correctness.rationale: For the exact telescoping shift, the q_0-th moment is the ℓ^r norm to the r-th power of a sum of nonnegative coordinate contribution vectors, with r=q_0/p=1/β. Minkowski gives an upper bound by the sum of their ℓ^r norms. Because βr=1, each coordinate contributes b_j A_{j,N}^β. The exact scalar supremum is sup_j A_{j,N}=NH_N, attained at j=N. Raising back to the r-th power gives the claimed upper bound, and e_N attains it. All parameter, countable-sum, and N=1 boundary cases were checked.
